links.note: The Indian Ocean bounded by Asia to the north, Africa to the west and Australia to the east - this concept's box gives exactly those limits.
Why the count of continents varies - this concept explains it case by case, Europe and Asia being one landmass but counted separately for historical and cultural reasons. Already linked and correct.
The tiny marine plants at the base of the ocean's life - this concept's marine flora, which it gives as tiny plants called algae and all kinds of seaweeds.
A blue whale as marine fauna - this concept's marine fauna is thousands of species of fish, dolphins, whales and deep-sea creatures, against the algae and seaweeds of the flora.
Almost three-fourths of the Earth's surface covered with water - this concept's figure. Already linked and correct.
A continent as a large continuous expanse of land - this concept's definition, set against a landmass.
The Indian Navy's motto Sam No Varunah, invoking the Vedic deity Varuna - this concept's DON'T MISS OUT box. Already linked and correct.
Freshwater found in glaciers, rivers, lakes, the atmosphere and underground as groundwater - this concept's list.
Five oceans observable on the world map - this concept's list. Already linked and correct.
The Arctic as the smallest of the oceans - the last place in this concept's order of size.
Flora as plant life - this concept introduces the term through the marine flora, the algae and seaweeds.
Fauna as animal life - this concept introduces the term through the marine fauna, the fish, dolphins, whales and deep-sea creatures.
The Arabian Sea to the west of India - this concept's box, with the Bay of Bengal to the east.
A tsunami as a huge and powerful wave generally caused by a strong earthquake or volcanic eruption at the bottom of the ocean - this concept's definition.
The 26 December 2004 tsunami around the Indian Ocean - this concept's case. Already linked and correct.
Seven continents as the list most widely adopted and used - this concept states it after tabulating the counts of four, five, six and seven.
Greenland as the largest island in the world - this concept's detail. Already linked and correct.
India's two major island groups, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and the Lakshadweep Islands - this concept names both, among India's more than 1,300 small islands.
Dakshin Gangotri, established in 1983 as India's first Antarctic base - this concept's account. Already linked and correct.
More than half of the world's oxygen produced by the oceans' flora, which is why they are called the planet's lungs - this concept's statement. Already linked and correct.
8 June designated World Oceans Day by the United Nations - this concept's closing sentence. Already linked and correct.
Threats to marine life - this concept names several million tonnes of plastic waste thrown into the oceans each year, other forms of pollution, and overfishing.
Why the Earth is called the blue planet - this concept's opening, that most of its surface is covered with water so it appears mostly blue from outer space.
Seawater being salty and unfit for consumption while freshwater is the small usable fraction - this concept's contrast.
